text: The Oak Street Library will hold a seed swap on Saturday, April 18, in its second-floor meeting room. Doors open at 10 a.m., and each visitor may take up to four packets. Bringing seeds is optional. Volunteers will have blank labels at the check-in table for anyone who brings unmarked packets.

claims.text: The seed swap takes place on Saturday, April 18.
Doors open at 10 a.m.
Each visitor can take at most four packets.
Visitors can participate without bringing seeds.

text: The Westbrook community center will move Friday's film screening to the gym because the courtyard is flooded. The film starts at 7:15 p.m., and visitors should enter through the west doors. Anyone who bought an outdoor ticket can use it in the gym. Folding chairs will be available near the back wall.

claims.text: The flooded courtyard is the reason the screening moves indoors.
The film starts at 7:15 p.m.
Visitors should use the west entrance.
Outdoor tickets remain valid in the gym.

text: A garden logger reads three soil probes every 15 minutes. It uploads readings when the wireless link is available. If the link fails, the logger stores the readings locally. Once the link returns, the logger sends its oldest stored readings first, so the dashboard can rebuild the missing part of its timeline.

claims.text: The logger reads three soil probes.
The logger reads the probes every 15 minutes.
The logger stores readings locally during a wireless outage.
The logger sends the oldest stored readings first after reconnecting.

text: The test rig uses a green lamp to show that a tray is ready. The lamp turns on only after the temperature remains below 30 degrees Celsius for five consecutive minutes. A single warmer reading resets the timer. The rig continues to record the temperature while the lamp is off.

claims.text: The temperature must be below 30 degrees Celsius for the tray to become ready.
The qualifying period lasts five consecutive minutes.
A single warmer reading resets the timer.
Temperature recording continues when the lamp is off.

text: Mina brought two umbrellas to meet her brother at the bus stop. The bus arrived twenty minutes late, by which time the rain had stopped. She lent the blue umbrella to a neighbor whose walk was longer, folded the yellow umbrella into her bag, and walked home with her brother.

claims.text: Mina brought two umbrellas.
The bus was twenty minutes late.
It had stopped raining before the bus arrived.
Mina lent the blue umbrella to a neighbor.

text: Andre discovered a brass key under the loose tile beside his aunt's back steps. He tried it on the garden shed, but it would not turn. His aunt recognized the key as the one for an old sewing box. She had moved the box to the upstairs closet the previous spring.

claims.text: Andre discovered the key under a loose tile by his aunt's back steps.
The key did not turn in the garden shed lock.
The key belongs to a sewing box.
Andre's aunt moved the sewing box to the upstairs closet the previous spring.

text: The Maple Avenue pool will open its east entrance at 8:30 a.m. on June 6 for a free swim clinic. The first session is reserved for children ages eight through twelve. A parent or guardian must stay on site throughout that session. The lifeguards will provide kickboards at the start of the lesson.

claims.text: The east entrance opens at 8:30 a.m. on June 6.
The first session is reserved for children ages eight through twelve.
A parent or guardian must remain on site throughout the first session.
The lifeguards provide kickboards.

text: The Pine Hill repair cafe will meet in Room 204 on February 7. Volunteers can look at lamps and small kitchen appliances, but they cannot accept microwaves. Visitors must claim a fifteen-minute time slot at the front desk. The desk opens half an hour before the first repair session begins.

claims.text: The repair cafe meets in Room 204.
Volunteers cannot accept microwaves.
Visitors must claim a fifteen-minute time slot.
The desk opens thirty minutes before the first repair session.

text: The Riverbend museum will offer a lantern walk on November 14. The group leaves the museum steps at dusk and follows the paved route to the footbridge. Visitors should bring a flashlight if they have one. If the river path closes because of flooding, the guide will lead a tour inside the museum instead.

claims.text: The walk is scheduled for November 14.
The group departs at dusk.
The planned outdoor route leads to the footbridge.
Closure due to flooding moves the tour inside the museum.

text: A mobile bookshop will stop at the Mercer Station parking lot on the second Tuesday of each month. It stays for two hours beginning at noon. Shoppers can trade at most three used books during a visit. The driver sets out a separate cart for books that people want to donate without making a trade.

claims.text: The stop occurs on the second Tuesday of each month.
The visit begins at noon and lasts two hours.
Each shopper can trade at most three used books per visit.
A separate cart is available for donations without a trade.

text: Registration for the Hilltop pottery workshop opens at 9 a.m. on September 2. The class meets three times in the arts building. All participants must attend the first meeting because the instructor demonstrates how to handle the kiln safely. Students may bring their own tools or borrow a basic set from the studio.

claims.text: Registration opens at 9 a.m. on September 2.
The class meets three times.
Attending the first meeting is mandatory for every participant.
Basic tool sets can be borrowed from the studio.

text: The Ash Street market starts using a new layout this Sunday. Produce sellers will set up in the north lot, and music will move under the covered walkway. The shuttle from City Hall stays on its thirty-minute schedule. Customers who walk in can still use either entrance during normal market hours.

claims.text: The new layout starts this Sunday.
Produce sellers will be in the north lot.
Music will move under the covered walkway.
The City Hall shuttle continues to run every thirty minutes.

text: The Fern County observatory will host an open night on August 21. Tickets cover entry between 8 and 10 p.m. The staff will put away the large telescope if lightning is visible, but the indoor exhibit will stay open. People who arrive by bicycle can use the racks beside the visitor center.

claims.text: Open night is on August 21.
Tickets cover entry between 8 and 10 p.m.
Staff will put away the large telescope if lightning is visible.
The indoor exhibit stays open if lightning is visible.

text: The Brook Lane school will collect coats in the front lobby from Monday through Thursday next week. Staff ask donors to put children's coats in the green bins. The blue bins are for adult coats. The school will send all donations to the shelter on Friday morning, after volunteers have sorted them by size.

claims.text: The school accepts donations from Monday through Thursday.
Children's coats go in the green bins.
Adult coats go in the blue bins.
Donations go to the shelter on Friday morning.

text: A parcel kiosk will keep a compartment locked for 48 hours after a courier scans a package. The recipient enters a six-digit code to open the door. If the code is entered incorrectly three times, the kiosk disables entry for five minutes. The timer does not shorten the package's collection window.

claims.text: The collection window is 48 hours from the courier scan.
The entry code has six digits.
Three incorrect entries trigger a five-minute lockout.
The lockout leaves the collection window unchanged.

text: The lake station records water depth once per minute. It saves the median of five readings to prevent a single passing boat from distorting the archive. An alert goes out when two consecutive saved values fall below 40 centimeters. Staff can view individual readings for the most recent hour on the station display.

claims.text: Water depth is measured once per minute.
The station saves the median of five measurements.
Two consecutive saved values below 40 centimeters trigger an alert.
The display shows individual readings from the most recent hour.

text: A classroom air monitor ignores its first two readings after power is restored because the sensor needs time to warm up. It then publishes one result every ten seconds. An amber light means the sensor needs service. If the network drops, the monitor continues to show results on its own screen.

claims.text: The first two readings after power is restored are discarded.
The monitor publishes one result every ten seconds after warm-up.
An amber light indicates the sensor needs service.
Results still appear on the monitor's screen during a network outage.

text: The library's scanner saves a preview before producing a full-resolution image. The preview is removed automatically at the end of the session, unless a staff member marks it for review. A saved full-resolution image goes into a folder named for the current date. The scanner opens a new folder at midnight.

claims.text: The scanner creates the preview before the full-resolution image.
Previews marked for review are kept beyond the session.
Full-resolution images go in a date-named folder.
The scanner opens a new folder at midnight.

text: The warehouse cart pauses for three seconds when a box crosses the painted lane. A floor sensor checks whether the lane is clear before the motor starts again. If the sensor stays blocked for more than thirty seconds, the cart sounds a short alarm and waits for someone to press the reset button.

claims.text: A box crossing the lane makes the cart pause for three seconds.
The motor checks for a clear lane using the floor sensor before restarting.
A blockage lasting more than thirty seconds triggers an alarm.
After the alarm, someone must press the reset button for the cart to continue.

text: A test pump draws water from the lower tank until its level reaches twelve centimeters. Once the pump stops, a valve keeps water from flowing back through the hose. The controller logs each shutdown with a timestamp. Turning off the display leaves both the controller and the pump in their current operating states.

claims.text: The pump stops drawing from the lower tank when the level reaches twelve centimeters.
The valve prevents backflow after the pump stops.
The controller records a timestamp for each shutdown.
Turning off the display does not change the pump or controller state.

text: The greenhouse vents open automatically when the interior grows warmer than 28 degrees Celsius. They stay open until the temperature falls below 25 degrees Celsius. The gap prevents the motors from starting repeatedly when the temperature hovers near one threshold. After sunset, the controller records the temperature but keeps the vents closed.

claims.text: Vents open automatically above 28 degrees Celsius.
Open vents stay open until the temperature drops below 25 degrees Celsius.
The two thresholds reduce repeated motor starts.
The controller keeps the vents closed after sunset.

text: The archive backs up new files every evening at six. For a file to be deleted automatically, it must have been in the temporary folder for at least seven days. A file flagged by a reviewer is protected from deletion. The archive produces a daily list of files removed by the cleanup job.

claims.text: New files are backed up each evening at six.
Automatic deletion requires at least seven days in the temporary folder.
A reviewer flag protects a file from deletion.
The archive lists files removed by cleanup each day.

text: Theo arrived at the bakery five minutes after it had closed. As he turned to leave, the baker tapped on the window and handed him a bag containing two rolls that would otherwise go to waste. Theo brought one roll to his sister and ate the other on the walk home.

claims.text: Theo arrived five minutes after closing.
The baker gave Theo two rolls.
Theo brought one roll to his sister.
Theo ate the other roll on the way home.

text: Carmen was halfway down the trail when she realized that her red notebook was still on the bench by the entrance. She asked Luis to wait at the trail marker while she went back. A volunteer had moved the notebook under the bench to keep it dry. Carmen found it before the rain got heavier.

claims.text: Carmen left a red notebook on the bench by the entrance.
Carmen asked Luis to wait at the trail marker.
A volunteer moved the notebook under the bench.
The volunteer moved the notebook to keep it dry.

text: When Farah sorted her grandfather's photographs, she found a ferry ticket dated May 3 tucked inside a sleeve. The photograph in that sleeve showed a bicycle leaning against a wall. Her grandfather explained that the ticket was from a trip he took the following week, so Farah filed the ticket and photo separately.

claims.text: The ferry ticket is dated May 3.
The photograph in the sleeve shows a bicycle leaning against a wall.
The ticket was from a trip the grandfather took the following week.
Farah filed the ticket separately from the photograph.

text: Inez promised to water Malik's plants while he was away for four days. On Tuesday she noticed that the clay pot was cracked, so she moved its plant into a spare pot. She left the other pots where they were and wrote Malik a note so he would know what had happened.

claims.text: Malik was away for four days.
Inez noticed the cracked clay pot on Tuesday.
Inez moved the plant from the cracked pot into a spare pot.
Inez left all the other pots where they were.

text: Jasper found his sister's scarf on the last seat of the bus. He put it in his backpack because she had lent it to him that morning. At the station he tried calling her twice, but her phone went to voicemail. He returned the scarf in person that evening.

claims.text: Jasper found the scarf on the last seat of the bus.
His sister had lent him the scarf that morning.
Jasper made two phone calls to his sister at the station.
Jasper returned the scarf in person that evening.

text: Marta was practicing a tune for Sunday's recital when the smallest string on her guitar snapped. The shop was already closed, so her neighbor lent her a guitar for the evening. She used her own guitar at the recital after replacing the string the next day. She returned the borrowed instrument on Monday.

claims.text: The recital was on Sunday.
The smallest string on Marta's guitar snapped.
Marta played her own guitar at the recital.
Marta returned the borrowed guitar on Monday.

text: Ravi planned to take the 6:40 train to meet his cousin for dinner. He reached the platform just as the train pulled away. Since the next departure was canceled, he took a bus downtown. His cousin saved him a seat by the window even though he was nearly an hour late.

claims.text: Ravi planned to take the 6:40 train.
The departure after the train he missed was canceled.
Ravi took a bus downtown.
Ravi's cousin saved him a seat by the window.

text: Bea took three jars of peach jam to her uncle's house. She dropped one in the driveway, and its glass broke before she reached the front door. Her uncle helped her clean it up. At dinner they opened one of the remaining jars and saved the other for her uncle's neighbor.

claims.text: Bea brought three jars of peach jam.
One jar broke in the driveway.
Bea's uncle helped clean up the broken jar.
They saved one intact jar for Bea's uncle's neighbor.
